What is in the template

How to fill it in

Before you start: are you VAT-registered?

This template shows VAT because many UK invoices need it. If you are not VAT-registered you must not charge VAT or show a VAT number. In that case set every VAT rate in the table to 0% (or delete the VAT column and VAT summary row in Word) and remove the VAT line from the From block. If you are unsure, check the registration rules and current rates on GOV.UK or ask your accountant. Nothing here is tax advice.

Step 1: Replace the From and Bill to details

Click each [bracketed] item and type over it. Use your full legal name or trading name, your address and your email. If you are VAT-registered, add your VAT number in the format shown. For limited companies, UK company law also expects the registered name and number to appear on business documents, so add your company number to the footer or the From block. For the client, use the name of the company or person you are billing, and the address the invoice should go to.

Step 2: Number and date it

Give every invoice a unique number from a sequence, such as INV-0001, INV-0002. Do not reuse or skip numbers without a reason, because gaps invite questions from accountants and tax authorities. Set the issue date to the day you send it. The due date is the issue date plus your payment terms; 30 days is common, but use whatever you agreed in writing. Put the client’s purchase order number in the PO field if they gave you one, since many accounts teams will not pay without it.

Step 3: Describe the work so it can be checked

Replace the sample rows. Write the description the way your client would recognise it (“Website copywriting, 12 pages”), then use the small grey line underneath for detail such as dates or scope. Enter the quantity, the unit (hour, day, item, project) and the price excluding VAT. Add the VAT rate for each line: 20% is the standard rate, some goods and services are at a reduced rate or zero-rated, and some are exempt. If you are not sure which applies, check GOV.UK before you send. Delete unused rows or copy a row to add more.

Step 4: Check the maths

In Word, the numbers are plain text, so Word will not recalculate them for you. After editing, work out each line (quantity × unit price), add the lines for the net total, multiply each VAT rate group to get the VAT, and add the two for the total. The sample works like this: £750.00 + £1,200.00 + £90.00 = £2,040.00 net; VAT at 20% on the £1,950.00 that is standard-rated is £390.00; total £2,430.00. If you would rather not do this by hand, a spreadsheet or the agent skill below does it for you and flags any mismatch.

Step 5: Add how to pay and save a PDF

Replace the sample bank details with your own account name, sort code and account number, and keep the reference equal to the invoice number so you can match the payment. Edit the note at the bottom to say what you agreed on late payment. Then use File > Save As > PDF and send the PDF, keeping the Word file for your records. Keep copies of all invoices for the period required by HMRC (check GOV.UK for how long).

What a UK VAT invoice normally has to show

HMRC’s guidance for a VAT invoice lists: a unique invoice number, your business name and address, your VAT number, the customer’s name and address, the invoice date, the date of supply if different, a description of what was supplied, the quantity and price, the VAT rate for each item, the total excluding VAT, the VAT amount and the total including VAT. This template covers all of these. Requirements change, so confirm against GOV.UK for your situation.

Frequently asked questions

Is this invoice template really free?

Yes. Download the Word and PDF files without giving an email address. Use them for your own business as often as you like.

Does it work in Google Docs or Pages?

The .docx opens in Word, LibreOffice, Google Docs and Pages. Check the spacing after you open it, because each app handles fonts slightly differently.

Can I add my logo?

Yes. The rounded box with your initials is a placeholder. In Word, delete it and insert your logo image in the same place.

Is it compliant with HMRC rules?

It includes the fields HMRC lists for a VAT invoice, but I cannot confirm it is right for your circumstances. Check GOV.UK or ask your accountant, especially for the VAT rates and any special schemes.

I am not VAT-registered. Can I still use it?

Yes. Set the VAT rates to 0% or delete the VAT column and summary row, and remove any VAT number.
